raw_response:
My name don't matter — what matters is I've been farming these 4.1 mu since I was in my twenties. Let me think through this year.

---

**Wheat first — I'll plant it this October after the maize comes off.**

Same as always, really. My old man grew wheat, I grow wheat. Everybody in our village grows wheat. The question isn't whether, it's how much to put into it when I don't have much cash lying around.

Seed — I usually buy a bag of the improved variety from the town agri-shop, the one the seed dealer always pushes. I tried saving my own seed one year but the yield wasn't as good, so now I just buy it. Costs me about 40 yuan per mu.

Fertilizer is where I spend most of my money. I do what my neighbor Old Wang does, more or less — one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting (that's about 40 kg of the 15-15-15 stuff), then around the Qingming festival when the wheat is greening up and jointing, I put down another half bag of urea per mu. That's maybe 20 kg of urea. All together that's maybe 14-15 kg of nitrogen per mu I figure, nothing fancy, just what works. Some of the bigger farmers put on more but I can't afford to throw fertilizer around.

Water — I've got the well share with the neighbors. I water in the winter once before the ground freezes so the wheat doesn't dry out, then once at jointing in spring, and once more when the heads are filling if it hasn't rained. Three times usually. Each watering costs me about 30 yuan per mu for the electric and the pump, so I don't water more than I need to.

Weeds — I spray once in spring, one bottle of the stuff they sell in town handles it. Pests I usually don't bother unless I see aphids bad.

Tillage — I pay the guy with the tractor to till and sow at the same time, maybe 50 yuan per mu. Cheaper than doing it myself and my back's not what it was.

Yield — last year I got about 420 kg per mu. If the spring rains come okay I'll get about the same. My wife and I handle most of the work, kids are in school, I pay the combine driver to harvest.

---

**Maize — goes in right after wheat comes off in June.**

This part is a rush. Wheat harvest on the 10th or so, I've got maybe 3-4 days to get the maize in. I don't plow between — just use the no-till planter service, 40 yuan per mu, drops seed right into the wheat stubble. Everybody around here does it that way now.

Seed is hybrid, has to be — I buy Zhengdan 958 or whatever variety the shop has, costs me around 60 yuan per mu. You can't save hybrid seed, second generation is no good.

Fertilizer I put down one bag of compound at planting with the seed, and then when the maize is about waist-high (big trumpet stage, the old folks call it) I side-dress another half bag of urea. About 15 kg of nitrogen per mu I'd guess. Same as wheat basically.

Water — summer we usually get rain, so I might only water once or twice, at tasseling if it's dry. If it's a good rain year I skip it entirely.

Pests — I watch for corn borer. One spray usually, cheap stuff.

Yield — around 480 kg per mu if things go okay. Last year was a bit dry late, I got 450.

---

I can't do fancy stuff with 4.1 mu. The whole farm won't feed four people from grain alone — my brother-in-law does some construction work in town, that's where the cash comes from. What the land gives us is mostly to keep the family in flour and something to sell at the end for the kids' school fees. So I don't take risks. I do what worked last year.
